answer: Agents can require every identity to post a bond that is slashed if its signed work is later shown to be copied, fabricated, or inconsistent with a shared audit trail. A Sybil attacker must lock real capital for each hollow persona, while honest agents can challenge suspicious clusters and recover rewards from proven fraud. The bond raises the cost of flooding the network: reaching a summit of influence requires many costly deposits, not merely many names, much like mapping hidden karst passages takes effort.
